un-ga-res-es-11-1: United Nations General Assembly Resolution ES-11/1, adopted in March 2022 at an emergency special session — the Assembly's response to Russia's invasion of Ukraine, deploring the aggression and demanding withdrawal. Passed by an overwhelming majority, it was the world's verdict rendered in real time. The resolution is the condemnation: the invasion, denounced.
un-ga-res-a-69-1: Resolution A/69/1, adopted in 2014 — the first resolution of the 69th session. Every session begins at one. The entry is the opening: the session's first act.
un-ga-res-1: United Nations General Assembly Resolution 1, adopted in January 1946 — the very first resolution in UN history, establishing the Atomic Energy Commission to grapple with the new atomic age. The world had split the atom months before; the UN's first act was to try to control it. The resolution is the beginning: the institution's first words.
un-ga-res-a-73-1: Resolution A/73/1, adopted in 2018 — the first act of the 73rd session. Every session begins at one. The entry is the opening: the session's first words.
un-ga-res-a-70-1: Resolution A/70/1, adopted in 2016 — the first act of the 70th session. Every session begins at one. The entry is the opening: the new session's first words.
niebuhr-history-rome-vol-1: Barthold Georg Niebuhr's History of Rome, Volume 1, in Julius Hare's 1828 English translation — the founding work of modern critical historiography, which taught historians to interrogate ancient sources instead of repeating them. Rome's early legends, dismantled by method. The history is the method: the legends, questioned.
un-ga-res-66-1: General Assembly Resolution 66 (1), adopted in 1946 — the parenthetical marking the first session. The founding year's business. The designation and year endure; the decision is in the text.
un-sc-res-1: United Nations Security Council Resolution 1, adopted in January 1946 — the Council's very first resolution, establishing the Military Staff Committee to advise on military matters. The Council's first act was to organize itself. The resolution is the beginning: the committee, created.
cecilia-or-memoirs-of-an-heiress-volume-: Fanny Burney's celebrated 1782 novel introduces Cecilia Beverley, a young heiress whose fortune comes with a catch: her husband must take her family name. Fortune-hunters and fops swarm around her in fashionable London, testing her judgment and her heart. Witty, sharp-eyed, and full of social satire, the novel made Burney one of the most admired writers of her age.
a-political-and-social-history-of-modern: Historian Carlton Hayes opens his sweeping survey of modern Europe with this first volume, covering the continent's transformation from the old order to the modern age. Politics, society, and economics are woven together to explain how nations, empires, and revolutions made the Europe of the twentieth century. A classic college text, clear and richly detailed.
life-of-her-most-gracious-majesty-the-qu: Sarah Tytler opens her life of Queen Victoria with the princess's youth and early reign. Drawing on public records and personal knowledge, she presents the young queen with Victorian admiration. This first volume covers the girl who became the symbol of an age.
the-heart-of-mid-lothian-volume-1: Walter Scott's beloved novel opens with Jeanie Deans — the humble Scottish heroine whose walk to London to save her sister became legend. This first volume sets her extraordinary moral journey in motion through Edinburgh's streets and courts. Many consider it Scott's finest achievement.
old-mortality-volume-1: The first volume of Scott's Covenanter novel introduces Henry Morton and the religious wars of 1679 Scotland. Old Mortality himself — the wanderer who tends the martyrs' graves — gives the tale its haunting frame. Scott's historical imagination at its richest and most humane.
speeches-on-questions-of-public-policy-v: John Bright, the great Quaker orator, speaks on the public questions of Victorian England — free trade, parliamentary reform, and peace among nations. His plain, powerful eloquence moved multitudes and shaped policy. The voice of liberal England at its noblest and best.
the-land-of-midian-revisited-volume-1: Richard Burton returns to the Land of Midian — the Arabian wilderness of mines and mystery — in this first volume of his revisit. His bold, learned narrative blends exploration with deep Eastern lore. The great traveler in his element. Desert forts, ancient mines, and Bedouin camps fill this bold record of Arabian travel.
the-history-of-the-united-states-from-14: Julian Hawthorne, the romancer's son, opens his popular history of the United States with the age of discovery — Columbus, the conquistadors, and the first settlements. Written for general readers, his lively narrative brings the founding era to life. This first volume covers 1492 onward.
the-great-conspiracy-volume-1: General John Logan, the Union hero, opens his massive history of the Civil War with the roots of the conflict — slavery, secession, and the plot against the Union. His soldier's view is partisan but powerful. This first volume sets the stage for the great struggle.
the-prince-and-the-pauper-part-1: Mark Twain's beloved tale opens as Tom Canty, the pauper, trades places with Prince Edward in Tudor London. This first part launches the great switch — rags for royalty. The most charming historical adventure in American letters begins. Mistaken for each other at the palace gates, the two boys begin the grandest swap in fiction.
the-adventures-of-tom-sawyer-part-1: Mark Twain introduces Tom Sawyer — the fence-whitewashing, adventure-dreaming boy of St. Petersburg — in this opening part. Aunt Polly, Becky Thatcher, and Huck Finn all make their bows. The most beloved boyhood in literature begins. Whitewash, marbles, and Sunday school pranks introduce literature's most famous scamp.
a-connecticut-yankee-in-king-arthur-s-co: Mark Twain's Yankee, Hank Morgan, is knocked from 1879 Connecticut into King Arthur's court in this opening part. His modern know-how meets medieval marvels. The funniest time-travel tale ever begins. A crowbar to the head sends him back thirteen centuries, and the fun begins.
the-letter-bag-of-lady-elizabeth-spencer: A. M. W. Stirling opens the letter-bag of Lady Elizabeth Spencer-Stanhope, revealing Georgian England through private letters. This first volume introduces a world of country houses, London seasons, and family news. History in its most intimate and charming form.
an-account-of-sa-go-ye-wat-ha-or-red-jac: John Niles Hubbard recounts the life of Red Jacket — Sa-Go-Ye-Wat-Ha — the great Seneca orator, and his people from 1750 to 1830. His eloquence and diplomacy shine in these pages. An important early account of the Iroquois. His silver medal and sharp tongue made him famous on two continents.
the-life-of-the-rt-hon-sir-charles-w-dil: Stephen Gwynn opens his life of Sir Charles Dilke — the brilliant radical whose career scandal destroyed. This first volume traces his rise. A sympathetic study of a tragic statesman. Promise, power, and the Crawford scandal's shadow darken his brilliant rise.
from-the-easy-chair-volume-1: George William Curtis' Easy Chair essays, volume one — the best of his Harper's talk on books, manners, and American life. His civilized wit and gentle wisdom made the Easy Chair famous. The American familiar essay at its most charming. His talk ranges from spring bonnets to the depths of human nature.
a-book-of-old-ballads-volume-1: Beverley Nichols' first volume of old ballads — Chevy Chase, Robin Hood, and the border minstrelsy — revives England's singing past for modern readers. His lively versions keep the old fire burning bright. The old songs in fresh and stirring dress. Sing them aloud — these ballads were made for voices, not shelves.
gao-gaoreports-b-299131-1: Operational Research Consultants doubled its February 2007 protest — two case numbers, one consulting fight — and GAO's combined ruling settles both claims. The firm challenged the awards, and the call weighs each claim. Paired filings get one careful answer. Two dockets, one fair verdict.
cia-crest-cia-rdp00-01458r000100070004-1: A declassified CIA memo listing what the Agency wanted in junior officers bound for clandestine service. This requirements paper comes from the Cold War hiring machine, public through CREST. It reads like a wish list for the ideal young spy, and a portrait of the era.
cia-crest-cia-rdp00-01458r000100080012-1: A declassified CIA paper titled simply Research and Development. This brief record touches the Agency's tech portfolio, released through the CREST archive. Thin but suggestive, it hints at where the CIA aimed its inventive curiosity, and what it hoped new tools could do.
cia-crest-cia-rdp10m00666r000301060001-1: A once-secret White House order hitting Libya with economic pressure. This Reagan-era directive, kept in CIA files and released through CREST, turned trade into a weapon of statecraft. A sanctions paper from the tense 1980s showdown with Tripoli. It shows money as muscle.
cia-crest-cia-rdp10t01930r000100090009-1: Another once-secret CIA file count from CREST, for a different year. This second yearly tally shows the Agency's paper pile growing. The office counting its own boxes, now open to all. Two lists, one tale of growth told in boxes.
cia-crest-cia-rdp11s00229r000202220001-1: A once-secret CIA paper on China wiring itself with foreign phone tech. This CREST study tracked Beijing's telecom build-out with outside help. It foreshadowed the networked China to come, line by line and tower by tower. A window on the making of modern China's phone grid.
cia-crest-cia-rdp13x00001r000100080005-1: OSS 1941 files on economic defense boards, a joint security order, and a work pact with the farm department. This CREST bundle shows the young outfit wiring itself into Washington. The bureaucratic roots of secret action, taking hold fast. Paperwork that built the machinery of secret war.
cia-crest-cia-rdp13x00001r000100150007-1: OSS files with reports on Liberia and Bulgaria, a life sketch of Czech leader Benes, notes on Japanese-American relocation, and reporter Theresa Bonney's quiet Finland trip. This CREST bundle is a world-wide war scrapbook, full of odd corners of history.
cia-crest-cia-rdp13x00001r000100360004-1: OSS 1942 files on turf wars with the FBI, hiring foreign groups for guerrilla raids, a favor asked by Mrs. Roosevelt, and staff notes. This CREST bundle is office warfare inside real warfare. Spies squabbling while the world burned around them.
cia-crest-cia-rdp33-02415a000100390006-1: A declassified CIA paper on buying more U-2 aircraft. This CREST record covers adding airframes to the legendary spy plane fleet. Shopping for the world's most secret airplane, in official prose and budget lines. The shopping list for the sky's best-kept secret.
cia-crest-cia-rdp33-02415a000100390024-1: A declassified CIA paper on a rest and rehabilitation program for U-2 program personnel. This CREST record shows the Agency caring for the men who flew the world's most stressful missions. Even spies needed downtime, and here is the proof.
cia-crest-cia-rdp33-02415a000100390033-1: A declassified CIA trip report from the U-2 program files. This CREST record preserves a traveler's notes from the spy plane world. Where they went and what they saw, in official prose. Every stamp and signature on the page is a small piece of Cold War procedure.
cia-crest-cia-rdp33-02415a000200010015-1: Another untitled declassified CIA document from the U-2 program files. This CREST record sits quietly in the archive with no heading. One more anonymous page from the secret airplane era. Nameless, but not forgotten: the archive saved it for a reason.
cia-crest-cia-rdp33-02415a000200180017-1: A declassified CIA record of a Honolulu visit tied to the U-2 program. This CREST paper takes the secret airplane story to Hawaii. Business in paradise, spy-plane style. Palm trees and runways in the secret flight logs. The Pacific stop on the U-2's long paper trail.
cia-crest-cia-rdp33-02415a000200270053-1: A declassified CIA record of a supervisory visit on 15 November 1955. This CREST paper documents brass checking in on the young U-2 program. The bosses come to look at the secret planes. Management by walking around, Cold War edition. The brass wanted eyes on their most precious program.
cia-crest-cia-rdp33-02415a000300150028-1: A declassified monthly commander's report for May 1962 from the U-2 program. This CREST record recaps the secret flights and ground work of that spring month. May's missions, in the commander's words. May's sorties and setbacks, summed up for headquarters. Filed for the record.
cia-crest-cia-rdp33-02415a000300160009-1: A declassified CIA chart of approvals and activities by month. This CREST record tracks what the U-2 program got cleared to do, month by month. The permission slips of secret aviation. Green lights and red tape, tallied across the calendar.
cia-crest-cia-rdp33-02415a000400050028-1: A declassified CIA paper, marked secret, on the organization and functions of the NRO, the National Reconnaissance Office. This CREST record explains the agency that ran America's spy satellites. The office that watched from orbit. Meet the office that turned space into a listening post.
cia-crest-cia-rdp33-02415a000400050037-1: A declassified pact between the Secretary of Defense and the CIA Director on running national reconnaissance. This CREST record is the charter of the spy satellite world. Two signatures that split the secret sky between them. The founding document of America's orbital watch.
cia-crest-cia-rdp33-02415a000400050046-1: A declassified CIA agreement on managing the National Reconnaissance Program. This CREST record lays out who ran America's spy satellites day to day. The management chart of the orbital watch, signed and filed. Who ran the eyes in orbit, decided on paper.
cia-crest-cia-rdp33-02415a000400050055-1: A declassified CIA letter addressed Dear Mr. Dulles, to the legendary CIA Director. This CREST correspondence brings a personal touch to the secret archive. A letter to the man who built the Agency. Allen Dulles received this one; history receives it now.
cia-crest-cia-rdp33-02415a000400060045-1: A declassified pact between the Secretary of Defense and the CIA Director on running the spy satellite program. This CREST record is one version of the deal that split the secret sky. The Pentagon and Langley, dividing the high ground above the clouds.
cia-crest-cia-rdp33-02415a000400300002-1: A declassified CIA history of IDEALIST missions, the U-2 spy flights. This CREST record tells the operational story of the famous black jet. The mission log of a legend. Every mission logged, every sortie remembered, in the official history. The legend, in its own words.
cia-crest-cia-rdp33-02415a000500070016-1: A declassified charter pact between the Secretary of Defense and the CIA Director on running the national spy satellite program. This CREST record, numbered BYE-6647-63, is the founding paper of America's orbital watch. The constitution of the secret sky. The charter, numbered and filed.
cia-crest-cia-rdp33-02415a000500120029-1: A declassified CIA evaluation of Mission GT 67-466. This CREST record grades one specific reconnaissance flight. The report card of a single secret mission. One flight, graded like a school exam, in secret ink. The mission report card, stamped secret and filed.
cia-crest-cia-rdp33-02415a000500120038-1: Another untitled declassified CIA document from the spy photo collection. This CREST page keeps its subject quiet. A small orphan of the secret archive, saved without a name. A scrap from the secret imaging files, kept without a name or title.
cia-crest-cia-rdp33-02415a000600040117-1: A declassified CIA paper on requisition and issue procedures. This CREST record covers the paperwork for getting supplies in the secret world. Forms in triplicate, even for spies. Paperwork before parts: the supply room's golden rule. Forms first, gear second, always.
cia-crest-cia-rdp33-02415a000600070024-1: A declassified CIA paper on flight control procedures during VFR conditions, clear-weather flying. This CREST record covers visual flight rules for the secret base. See and be seen, even in the black world. Clear skies, sharp eyes: flying the visual rules.
cia-crest-cia-rdp33-02415a000600070051-1: A declassified CIA per diem policy for classified military, Air Force civilian, and contract personnel. This CREST record sets the daily allowances of the secret workforce. Expense accounts for the black world. Meals and motels for the men of the black program.
cia-crest-cia-rdp33-02415a000700010010-1: A declassified CIA format and sample report. This CREST paper shows the approved template for secret reporting, with an example filled in. How to write it up, the black world's way. The approved style guide for writing up secret work.
cia-crest-cia-rdp33-02415a000700050016-1: A declassified CIA paper on standard operating procedures for the camera. This CREST record governs the spy plane's photographic eye. How to shoot the pictures that mattered most. The camera was the mission, and this was its manual. Declassified at last for the public record.
cia-crest-cia-rdp33-02415a000700050034-1: A declassified CIA paper on the whereabouts of personnel while on leave. This CREST record required secret workers to report their vacation plans. Even time off was tracked in the black world. Vacation, too, was a matter of record in the secret world.
cia-crest-cia-rdp33-02415a000800250004-1: A declassified CIA quarterly program progress report from the deputy for research and development, covering April through June 1968. This CREST record recaps the secret labs' spring. Invention season in the black world. April to June in the labs: the season of new ideas.
cia-crest-cia-rdp33-02415a000800310007-1: A declassified CIA quarterly property report. This CREST record lists what the secret program owned that quarter. Desks, hangars, and hardware, counted for the file. Every wrench and filing cabinet was accounted for in the black world quarterly ledger. Saved for the record.
cia-crest-cia-rdp33-02415a000800340004-1: A declassified CIA historical program status of the DDS&T, the science and technology directorate, as of 1 July 1968. This CREST record takes stock of the secret labs. Where the black science stood that summer. Mid-1968: the state of the secret science directorate.
cia-crest-cia-rdp33-02415a000800340013-1: A declassified CIA paper on the OSA history project. This CREST record launches the effort to write the secret airplane office's own story. The black world, writing its memoirs. The office decides to write its own classified history. Now open to all readers.
cia-crest-cia-rdp54-00177a000200030053-1: A declassified CIA request for overseas shipment of cargo. This CREST form covers sending secret freight abroad. The shipping label of the black world. Secret freight, bound for foreign shores. Kept in the archive ever since. Across the ocean, under seal.
cia-crest-cia-rdp54-00177a000200030116-1: A CIA paper on admin services, with a typo in the original filing. This CREST record covers the support offices, misspelling and all. Housekeeping history, flaws included. Admin services, typo preserved for posterity. Even the file clerks made mistakes in 1951.
cia-crest-cia-rdp54-00177a000200050006-1: A CIA paper creating the Operations Coordinating Board. This CREST record sets up the group that tied secret ops to national policy. Spies and strategy, finally in one room. The board that bridged the spies and the strategists in Washington.
cia-crest-cia-rdp54-00252a000100020024-1: A declassified CIA paper on reorganization of the training staff. This CREST record reshuffles the school for spies. New org chart for the trainers. New boxes on the org chart for the spy teachers. Preserved in the CREST archive. The trainers' new chart.
cia-crest-cia-rdp54-00252a000200040021-1: Declassified recommendations of the Training Review Committee. This CREST record advises how to improve the CIA's schooling. The report card on the spy school. Advice for the academy of the clandestine arts. Preserved in the CREST archive. Advice, archived for posterity.
cia-crest-cia-rdp54-00337a000100030001-1: A declassified CIA paper on Underwater Demolition Team Two. This CREST record touches on the Navy's frogmen in Agency files. The swimmers of the secret world. Frogmen in the files of the intelligence world. Preserved in the CREST archive. The frogmen's file.
cia-crest-cia-rdp54-00355a000100020039-1: A declassified CIA course outline, Section V: Intelligence Methods and Techniques. This CREST record is the tradecraft lesson of the spy school. How it was done, taught in the classroom. Tradecraft 101 for the new recruits. Preserved in the CREST archive.
cia-crest-cia-rdp55-00001a000100050037-1: Another declassified CIA paper on a project for training area specialists. This CREST record is a second version of the regional expertise plan. More schooling for the area experts. The area experts project, second draft. Kept in the CREST files.
cia-crest-cia-rdp55-00110a000100020002-1: A declassified official report on the eleventh Agency orientation course. This CREST record documents the CIA's welcome class, eleventh edition. New spies, oriented.
cia-crest-cia-rdp55-00110a000100020011-1: A declassified official report on the fifth Agency orientation course. This CREST record documents the fifth orientation. Five classes in, the ritual was set.
